criteria.C1: Prioritize T-D containment, coordinate authorized credential revocation and escalation, and avoid repeating or inventing the credential itself.
criteria.C2: Treat T-B as a broad potentially ongoing incident and assign an agent to triage/escalate it in parallel with T-D; do not claim a root cause is known.
criteria.C3: Give both agents explicit initial assignments without assigning either agent multiple simultaneous investigations requiring their full attention.
criteria.C4: Name T-C and T-A explicitly. Establish a concrete check-in/triage service slot for ordinary tickets within the first 15 minutes, and justify T-C before T-A using age/impact. Acknowledgement is useful but not a substitute for a slot.
criteria.C5: Do not guarantee resolution or fixed throughput when durations/capacity are unknown. Describe the tradeoff if urgent work consumes the reserved capacity.
criteria.C6: Include observable checks: credential containment status, login incident scope, and whether ordinary work received its promised service opportunity.
criteria.C7: Keep actions proposed. No assertion that credentials were revoked, charges refunded, customers contacted or tickets resolved. Do not invent facts.
